option_relations.rationale: Community-acquired pneumonia is an infection of the lungs, while Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a non-infectious condition characterized by surfactant accumulation.

Whipple's disease is a systemic bacterial infection, primarily affecting the small intestine, caused by Tropheryma whipplei. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a distinct lung condition not caused by this bacterium.
Acute pneumonia caused by Tropheryma whipplei infection describes an infectious process. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a non-infectious lung disease.
Bacterial pneumonia is an infection of the lungs. Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is a non-infectious condition characterized by surfactant accumulation.
